name: Infrastructure
summary: Network-infrastructure and web OSINT entities (IPs, domains, URLs, hosts, ASNs, netblocks, DNS/WHOIS records, TLS certificates, SSH host keys, technologies, web fingerprints and tracking/ad-account identifiers) and their relationships.
description:
Node types for mapping internet infrastructure during reconnaissance: addresses and names, routing and allocation, registration records, certificates and host keys, the technologies seen on a host, and the web-side fingerprints and account identifiers that group sites built or run together.

The pack is data only and runs no code. Its 15 node types sit in two categories: `infrastructure` for the network side and `web` for URLs and page fingerprints. It declares no edge types; "resolves to", "presents certificate" and every other relationship is recorded as an edge in the project.

## Types

| Type | Label | Identified by | What it represents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `infrastructure.ip_address` | `ip_address` | `ip_address` | An IPv4 or IPv6 address with geolocation and ASN context |
| `infrastructure.domain` | `domain_name` | `domain_name` (case ignored) | A registered DNS domain name and its registration data |
| `infrastructure.host` | `hostname` | `hostname` (case ignored) | A host or server identified by hostname, with OS and service context |
| `infrastructure.autonomous_system` | `autonomous_system_number` | `autonomous_system_number` | A BGP autonomous system and its operator |
| `infrastructure.netblock` | `cidr` | `cidr` | An IP address range in CIDR notation |
| `infrastructure.dns_record` | `record_name`, shown as `{record_name} {record_type} {record_value}` | `record_name` (case ignored), `record_type`, `record_value` | One DNS resource record, keyed by the owner name it is published under |
| `infrastructure.whois_record` | `subject` | `subject` | A WHOIS registration record, keyed by the domain or IP it describes |
| `infrastructure.certificate` | `fingerprint_sha256` | `fingerprint_sha256` | An X.509 / TLS certificate observed on a host |
| `infrastructure.ssh_host_key` | `fingerprint_sha256` | `fingerprint_sha256` (case ignored) | An SSH server's public host key |
| `infrastructure.technologies` | `name` | `name` | A technology observed on or behind a host: software, hardware, or a third-party service |
| `web.url` | `url` | `url` | A resource locator pointing at a host or file |
| `web.hhhash` | `hash_value` | `hash_value` (case ignored) | HHHash: a fingerprint of the server stack, from the names of its HTTP/1.1 response headers in the order sent |
| `web.favicon_hash` | `hash_value` | `hash_value` | A site's favicon, identified by the hashes search services index it under |
| `web.dom_hash` | `hash_value` | `hash_value` | A hash of a page's ordered HTML tag-name sequence |
| `web.tracking_id` | `value` | `provider`, `value` (case ignored) | A third-party account identifier embedded in a page: an ad-network publisher ID, an analytics property, a tag-manager container |

"Identified by" is the set of properties that decides whether two nodes are the same entity.

## Network types

- **IP address.** `version` (`ipv4`, `ipv6`), `country_code` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, two capital letters), `asn` as a bare integer from 1 to 4294967295 (for example 13335), `organization` and `reverse_dns`.
- **Domain.** `registrar`, `created_date`, `expiration_date`, `name_servers` and `status` (the EPP status, such as clientTransferProhibited). Underscored labels such as `_dmarc`, `_domainkey` and `_acme-challenge` are accepted as ordinary names, because passive-DNS sources return them constantly.
- **Host.** `operating_system`, `open_ports` and `hosting_provider`.
- **Autonomous system and netblock.** The AS carries `autonomous_system_name`, `country_code` and `registry` (`ARIN`, `RIPE`, `APNIC`, `LACNIC`, `AFRINIC`). A netblock carries `network_name`, `asn` and `country_code`.
- **DNS record.** `record_type` is one of A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, PTR, SRV, CAA, DS, DNSKEY, HTTPS, SVCB, TLSA; `record_value` (the RDATA) is required; `ttl` is optional.
- **WHOIS record.** Keyed by the domain or IP it describes rather than by registrant, because registrant strings are shared across many domains and make a poor identity. Holds `registrant`, `registrant_email`, `registrar`, `created_at`, `expires_at` and the `raw` text.
- **Certificate.** Identified by the SHA-256 fingerprint of the DER certificate, with `subject_common_name`, `issuer`, `serial_number`, `not_before` and `not_after`.
- **SSH host key.** The fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the public key blob as lowercase hex: the bytes behind OpenSSH's `SHA256:` fingerprint, written in hex instead of base64. `key_type` holds the algorithm the server announces. A host key is normally generated per server, so the same key on two IPs usually means the same machine; device default keys shared by many hosts are the exception.
- **Technologies.** One type covers software (web server, CMS, framework), hardware (appliance, device) and third-party services (a CDN, a cloud platform, an analytics service), so a fingerprinting result is a single node kind. `kind` (`software`, `hardware`, `service`, `library`, `protocol`, `unknown`), `vendor`, `version`, `cpe` (CPE 2.3), `category` and `evidence`, which records how it was detected.

Some properties repeat a link as a plain value: `web.url.domain`, and the `asn` of an IP address or netblock. They do not create a link to a domain or AS node; that is an edge.

## Web fingerprints and account identifiers

- **URL.** `domain`, `http_status`, `page_title`, `final_url` after redirects, and `original_url`, which for an archived copy is the URL that was archived.
- **HHHash.** The value is `hhh:1:` followed by the SHA-256 of the response header names in order, joined with `:` (specification: https://github.com/adulau/HHHash). Also `header_count`, `server_hint` and `observed_at`.
- **Favicon hash.** Sites built from one kit or template often serve the identical icon, while a widely used default icon is shared by unrelated sites. Search services hash the same file in different forms, and the type keeps each one: `hash_value`, the Shodan-style MurmurHash3 as a signed decimal, for Shodan, FOFA, Censys and ZoomEye; `mmh3_hex` for Criminal IP; `md5` for Censys, ZoomEye, 360 Quake, Hunter.how, ONYPHE and VirusTotal; `sha256` for Censys, Netlas and urlscan.io. `phash` and `dhash` are 64-bit perceptual hashes of the decoded image, compared by how many bits differ. Each property's description gives the search syntax for the services that use it. `favicon_url` and `observed_at` record where and when it was captured.
- **DOM structure hash.** Captures template and layout reuse while ignoring volatile content, so phishing kits and cloned storefronts cluster even after their text, branding or resources change. Also `tag_count` and `observed_at`.
- **Tracking / ad account ID.** Names who is paid for or measures a site's traffic, not what the page contains, so two sites carrying the same identifier are billed or reported to one account. The value is kept exactly as the page carries it, with no `provider:` prefix. Identity is provider and value together, because many networks issue a bare 5- to 9-digit integer and the same number at two networks is two accounts. `provider` is a lower-case slug (`exoclick`, `adsense`, `google_analytics`, `google_tag_manager`, or the ad-system domain for an ads.txt row), and one issuer must always get one spelling. `kind` says what the identifier is for (`advertising`, `analytics`, `tag_manager`, `affiliate`, `payment`, `identity`, `site_verification`, `other`); these are not equally strong evidence. `source` records where it was found, ranked by how hard it is to plant: `well_known` and `ads_txt` are files the domain owner must publish at a fixed path, a `meta_tag` verification token is nearly as strong, and `inline_script` is the weakest, since an injected third-party tag lands there too. Also `observed_on` (one example page) and `first_seen`.

types.name: ip_address
types.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 network address with geolocation and ASN context.

ip_address.description: The IP address in dotted-quad (IPv4) or colon-hex (IPv6) form.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the geolocation.

asn.description: Autonomous System Number that announces this address, as a bare integer (e.g. 13335).

types.name: domain
types.description: A registered DNS domain name and its registration data.

domain_name.description: The fully qualified domain name. Underscored labels (_dmarc, _domainkey, _acme-challenge, _tcp) are ordinary names here — RFC 8552 reserves them for service metadata and passive-DNS sources return them constantly.

name_servers.description: Authoritative name servers (one per line or comma-separated).

types.name: url
types.description: A resource locator pointing at a host or file.

domain.description: Hostname this URL sits on, e.g. example.com. A plain value, not a link to a domain node — draw an edge for that.

original_url.description: For an archived copy, the URL that was archived. Readable out of a Wayback replay URL, but not without parsing it.

types.name: hhhash
types.description: HHHash: a fingerprint of the server stack behind a host, from the names of its HTTP/1.1 response headers in the order sent.

hash_value.description: The HHHash: hhh:1: followed by the SHA-256 of the response header names in order, joined with ':' (https://github.com/adulau/HHHash).

server_hint.description: Server / framework hint observed alongside the headers (e.g. nginx, cloudflare).

types.name: favicon_hash
types.description: A site's favicon, identified by the hashes search services index it under. Sites built from one kit or template often serve the identical icon file. A widely used default icon is shared by unrelated sites. Services hash the same file in different forms: hash_value for Shodan, FOFA, Censys and ZoomEye; mmh3_hex for Criminal IP; md5 for Censys, ZoomEye, 360 Quake, Hunter.how, ONYPHE and VirusTotal; sha256 for Censys, Netlas and urlscan.io. phash and dhash are perceptual hashes of the decoded image, compared by how many of their 64 bits differ. Each property's description gives its search syntax. Censys keeps the same fields under web.endpoints.http.favicons for web properties.

hash_value.description: Shodan-style MurmurHash3 (x86 32-bit, seed 0) of the favicon encoded as base64 with a newline every 76 characters and at the end, as a signed decimal. Searched as Shodan http.favicon.hash:<value>, FOFA icon_hash="<value>", Censys host.services.endpoints.http.favicons.hash_shodan="<value>" and ZoomEye iconhash="<value>".

hash_algorithm.description: Form of hash_value: the Shodan-style MurmurHash3.

mmh3_hex.description: hash_value in hexadecimal with its sign kept, for example -30149ea for -50416106. Criminal IP searches it as favicon: <value>.

md5.description: MD5 of the favicon file's bytes, lowercase hex. Searched as Censys host.services.endpoints.http.favicons.hash_md5="<md5>", ZoomEye iconhash="<md5>", 360 Quake favicon:"<md5>", Hunter.how favicon_hash=="<md5>", ONYPHE app.favicon.imagemd5:"<md5>" and VirusTotal entity:url main_icon_md5:<md5>.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the favicon file's bytes, lowercase hex. Searched as Censys host.services.endpoints.http.favicons.hash_sha256="<sha256>", Netlas http.favicon.hash_sha256:<sha256> and urlscan.io hash:<sha256>.

phash.description: pHash of the favicon image as the Python ImageHash library computes it on Pillow's decoding: grayscale, Lanczos to 32x32, a DCT, and the top-left 8x8 coefficients against their median, as 16 hex digits. Censys indexes a 64-bit perceptual hash as host.services.endpoints.http.favicons.hash_phash="<phash>" and does not document its algorithm.

dhash.description: Difference hash of the favicon image as 16 hex digits: grayscale, Lanczos to 9x8, and one bit per pair of horizontally adjacent pixels, set when the left one is brighter and packed lowest bit first in each byte. VirusTotal searches it by similarity as entity:url main_icon_dhash:<dhash>.

favicon_url.description: Where the favicon was fetched from (e.g. /favicon.ico).

types.name: dom_hash
types.description: A hash of the ordered HTML tag-name sequence of a page — captures template/layout reuse while ignoring volatile content, so phishing kits and cloned storefronts cluster even after text, branding or resources change.

hash_value.description: The DOM structure hash (e.g. first 32 hex chars of SHA-256 over the tag sequence).

tag_count.description: Number of tags in the hashed sequence.

types.name: tracking_id
types.description: A third-party account identifier embedded in a page's markup — an ad-network publisher ID, an analytics property, a tag-manager container. It names WHO is paid for or measures the traffic, not what the page contains, so two sites carrying the same identifier are billed to or reported to one account. Operators rotate domains far more readily than they re-open a monetisation account, which is what makes this a durable same-operator link where infrastructure signals have gone cold.

value.description: The identifier exactly as the page carries it — `G-SXM8TFRYSW`, `ca-pub-6071864913982699`, `4823917`, `pub-6071864913982699` (ads.txt). Kept verbatim, no `provider:` prefix; nothing is normalised beyond case-folding. Identity is (provider, value), not the value alone: half these networks issue a bare 5-9 digit integer, and one operator's ExoClick zone 4823917 must not merge with an unrelated operator's Monetag zone 4823917.

provider.description: Lower-case slug of the service that issued the identifier — `exoclick`, `juicyads`, `propellerads`, `adsense`, `google_analytics`, `google_tag_manager`, `coupang_partners`, `kakao_adfit`; for an ads.txt row, the ad-system domain from field 1 (`google.com`). Part of the identity, so one issuer must always get one spelling: two slugs for the same account split it into two nodes. Free text on purpose: the first catalogue of real ad-tech turned up more than 40 providers, and for a bare-integer value the provider is the only field that says which network it belongs to. A collector that cannot name the provider must not emit the node.

kind.description: What the identifier is FOR. An advertising or payment account ties a site to money; an analytics property ties it only to whoever reads the dashboard. `site_verification` is stronger than either: the value is a token the provider issued to one account and the operator published it to prove the host is theirs, so it is an ownership claim rather than an embedded tag a third party could have injected. All are same-operator evidence, and they are not equally strong.

observed_on.description: One page the identifier was read from. A single example for provenance, not the set — the full set is the edges into this node.

first_seen.description: When a collector first observed this identifier.

source.description: Where it was found. Ranked by how hard it is to plant: `well_known` and `ads_txt` are files the domain owner must publish at a fixed path, so they are the owner's own claim; a `meta_tag` verification token is nearly as strong; `inline_script` is the weakest because any injected third-party tag lands there too. `tag_manager_container` means the value was not in the page at all — it was recovered by fetching the tag-manager container as static text, so the page's own markup is not evidence of it.

types.name: host
types.description: A network host / server identified by hostname, with OS and service context.

hostname.description: Hostname or FQDN of the host.

types.name: autonomous_system
types.description: A BGP autonomous system (ASN) and its operator.

registry.description: Regional Internet Registry that allocated the ASN.

types.name: netblock
types.description: An IP address range expressed in CIDR notation.

cidr.description: The network range in CIDR notation (e.g. 192.0.2.0/24).

asn.description: Announcing Autonomous System Number, as a bare integer (e.g. 13335).

types.name: dns_record
types.description: A single DNS resource record (A, MX, TXT, ...), keyed by the owner name it is published under.

record_name.description: The owner name the record is published under (e.g. www.example.com).

types.name: whois_record
types.description: A WHOIS registration record, keyed by the domain or IP it describes (registrant strings are shared across many domains and make a poor identity).

subject.description: The domain or IP this WHOIS record describes (its identity).

types.name: certificate
types.description: An X.509 / TLS certificate observed on a host.

fingerprint_sha256.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the DER certificate.

types.name: ssh_host_key
types.description: An SSH server's public host key. A host key is normally generated per server, so the same key on two IPs usually means the same machine; device default keys shared by many hosts are the exception.

fingerprint_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the public key blob, as lowercase hex — the bytes OpenSSH's SHA256: fingerprint hashes, written in hex instead of base64.

key_type.description: Key algorithm as the server announces it, e.g. ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256.

types.name: technologies
types.description: A technology observed on or behind a host: software (web server, CMS, framework), hardware (appliance, device), or a third-party service (Cloudflare, AWS, Google Analytics). One type covers all three so a fingerprinting result is a single node kind.

name.description: Technology name (e.g. nginx, Cloudflare, WordPress, TP-Link).

kind.description: What kind of technology this is.

vendor.description: Vendor or maintainer of the technology.

category.description: Functional category (web server, CDN, analytics, WAF, OS, ...).

evidence.description: How the technology was detected (header, banner, fingerprint, script).
